Climdev fund togehter with AU and UNECA

The ClimDev-Africa Special Fund (CDSF) is the investment instrument of the ClimDev-Africa Programme and supports the building of resilience to the impacts of climate change in Africa. Specifically, CDSF supports African institutions to implement activities in three result areas: 1) Widely available Climate information, packaging and dissemination; 2) Quality analysis for decision support and management practice; 3) Informed decision-making, awareness and advocacy. CDSF was at the onset of the programme considered "a flagship programme for Africa" within Climate and Environment due to the composition of the programme with UNECA(ACPC) on the policy level, the AUC (DREA) at the political level and AfDB (CDSF) as the financial arm of the programme. Sida has been supporting the ClimDev Special Fund (CDSF, administered by AfDB) since its inception in 2013. Both allocations and disbursements from the fund have been slower than anticipated but now the fund is adequately staffed and its administration is well integrated with AfDB's overall work on climate change. CDSF is recognized as an important instrument for promoting climate services and innovative climate adaptation action across the continent. The fund and its staff are also instrumental in driving the climate change agenda within AfDB and using the Bank’s convening power and mandate to influence actors across the continent. As of November 2018, the funding provided to CDSF by Sida (75 MSEK) has been allocated and there is strong demand for additional for both 2018 and 2019. This demand has led AfDB to request additional short-term support from Sida to allow for continued project support to the end of 2019. The Swedish funding would be allocated according to the operational principles of CDSF and the rules and regulations of the Bank. In its request for additional funding from Sida the Bank outlines three areas where these funds will be invested: · Enhance the capacity of river basin organizations to deliver climate, weather and water services· Develop climate information services with high-resolution data and deliver climate services in flood and drought prone ecosystems· Policy and partnerships for the delivery of climate information services linking climate centers with regional operations for disaster risk planning These areas are a subset of the areas of interventions as outlined by the instrument establishing CDSF and are in line with the current strategy for Regional development cooperation – specifically results on and two of support area one. Increasing Sida’s support to CDSF and continuing to engage with AfDB on matters related to climate change is seen as an opportunity to capitalize on the long term support to ClimDev and benefit from the capacity that has been developed within the Bank for the administration of the fund.

The ClimDev Special Fund has been operational since 2014 and received grants form European Commission, Sweden and the Nordic Development Fund.
The CDSF has to date, launched one call for proposal in 2014, out of which 18 projects were approved. As of 31 December 2021, four projects were ongoing, while fourteen other projects are at various stages of completion. As of 31st December 2021, the Fund had disbursed €3.1 million for the year, bringing cumulative disbursements to €26.6 million out of the €34.4 million in committed Funds.
CDSF projects are categorized into three groups: (i) The Satellite and Weather Information for Disaster Resilience in Africa (SAWIDRA) projects. (ii) Multi-country projects; and (iii) Country-based projects.
In 2021:
At Regional level, the Fund operationalized two regional climate centers.
1) The IGAD center that serves nine countries in the Horn of Africa, with High Computing Clusters that now allow the Center to undertake advanced modelling that combines weather observation and remote sensed data to track desert locust breeding grounds and movements. The Center also advises countries and agencies on where to target control measures to limit damage to farmlands.
2) CAPC, the new ECCAS center established in Douala, Cameroon, was supported by a complement of coordination staff to manage the equipment installation and run the first operations for 11 countries in the central African region.
Multi-country initiaitve:
The CDSF has one ongoing multi-country project, Climate Data Rescue and Database Enhancement for improved Climate Information Services in National Meteorological and Hydrological Services (NMHSs) in Eastern and Southern Africa implemented by the WMO. In 2021, the project granted a no-cost extension until June 30, 2022, and realigned the project activities and budget to enable the PIU complete procurement and training activities
Country level operations:
1) Through its Amélioration de la résilience des populations par un meilleur accès à linformation climatique, the Fund is helping the Government of Côte dIvoire build resilience to climate change by improving access and use of climate information for decision-making to promote and pilot adaptation practices.
2) The project Renforcement des investissements pour un developpement resilient au changement climatique dans le complexe lac nokoue - lagune de Porto Novo in Benin. For the period 2021, the project carried out the following activities: Created a risk mapping tool; Study on climatic impacts on the production sectors (fishing, agriculture, health, river transport) and the degree of consideration of these impacts; Trained over 150 user representatives, and 30 local executives (including local authorities) trained; Two improved local contingency plans; Established a platform and the holding of 24 sessions; Created a meteorological and hydrological database.
3) Climate Change Adaptation in Northern Ghana Enhanced project implemented by the CFTC. Project activities and achievements for 2021 include: Completed training in 17 communities, and 1,215 smallholder farmers (comprising 401 men and 814 women) are accessing climate and seasonal weather information; Approved procurement of additional Three (3) Automatic Weathers Stations (AWS); One Thousand, One Hundred, and Thirty-Seven (1137) smallholder farmers (55% women) were trained and introduced to various climate-resilient agricultural practices on their farms.
4 The Enhancement of Data Collection and Sharing for Effective Water-Related Disaster Management in Zimbabwe aims to generate climatic data for water-related disaster management in Muzarabani, Gokwe, Tsholotsho, and Mwenezi Districts to counter the impacts of climate change. Project activities and achievements for 2021 include: The approval of the field situation assessment and procurement and installation of Hydromet equipment that will benefit Zimbabwe National Water Authority (ZINWA), the Meteorological Services Department, and four districts.
5) Disaster Risk Assessment and Climate Change Adaptation Project in Somalia, implemented by ICPAC on behalf of the Government of Somalia, aims to build the capacity of the National Meteorological Agency in climate early warning and demonstrate its benefits in building resilience and adapting to climate variability. The project reported the following activities and results: Approved a budget realignment to purchase and install four (4) automatic stations in the regions where ICPAC is already implementing the Rural Livelihoods Adaptation to Climate Change in the Horn of Africa (RLACC II) project; Facilitated a six-month training course on Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation with Data Management for six (6) staff from the Somalia Meteorological department at the Institute for Meteorological Training and Research (IMTR) in Kenya; Sponsored two students to undertake Post Graduate Diploma Course in Meteorology at the University of Dar es Salaam in November 2021.
6) Climate and Database Enhancement for Improved Climate Information Services (DARE) project seeks to contribute to improved climate data availability for climate change analysis and adaptation for improved climate services and food security in Djibouti, Swaziland, Uganda, and Zambia. The project reported the following activities and results in the reporting year:
The Climsoft software has been rolled out and currently used in 16 African National Meteorological and Hydrological Services (NMHSs); A joint Climsoft, Climate Data Management System and R-Instat, Climate Data Analysis Training workshop were organised and held from 29 November to 03 December 2021 and from 21-25 February 2022 respectively. More than 40 participants from 21 NMHS in Africa attended the workshop to acquire technical skills in climate data management and data analysis using both Climsoft and R-Instat softwares. Climate data managers in these 21 NMHSs have now been trained in both climate data analysis as well as in the use of the Climsoft software; A Policy-makers workshop in climate data rescue and services was organised and held from 26-28 January 2022 to enhance awareness of policy makers on existing climate products and services and their provisions by the NMHSs for participants from Djibouti, Eswatini, Uganda and Zambia.
Challenge faced by the fund during the reporting period (Jan - Dec 2021)
The Fund faced fundamental challenges in implementing its 2021 Work Program brought on by the 2020 global COVID-19 pandemic. These challenges included significant delays in procuring, installing, and testing critical climate and weather equipment for the regional climate center and the national meteorological and hydrological services (NMHS). It also includes the Funds inability to undertake missions to identify new projects, supervise ongoing projects, conduct audits, or mobilize resources.
